applies_why: The judge text addresses a collision between the challenger's own chain (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) and Matthew 1:20, then invokes Matthew 1:20's own words to resolve the point.
quote: the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: never verse by verse — reading one: the judge may not use Matthew 1:20's own wording as the decisive test; reading two: the judge may mention it only within a chain-against-chain footing.
why: The judge acknowledges the challenger's own-chain analogy is footed but then relies on the pressed sentence's own words, rather than weighing the two chains by footing as K-C requires.
